result:
The adapter returns **516 Black-owned firms** from the raw file, and all 16 tests pass. I wrote `adapter.py`, `test_adapter.py` and `NOTES.md`.

**Which firms count as Black-owned:** only one column in the file records the owner's race, `class_description_detailed`, and I kept rows where it says exactly `Black American`. That's 1,001 of the 7,935 rows, which matches the total the state publishes. I didn't use the MBE certification type as a signal, because it covers every minority group and many MBE rows say "No minority race/ethnicity identified."

**Why 1,001 rows become 516 firms:**
- **One row per certification period:** most firms appear several times, once each time they renewed.
- **Duplicated certifications:** many certification rows appear two or three times, identical except for the vendor ID in the detail link. It looks like an error in the export itself.

To handle this, I group rows that share a vendor ID or the same business name (ignoring case and punctuation). The 1,001 rows had 534 distinct vendor IDs, and 18 of those were duplicate IDs for a firm already counted. In the 35 cases where a firm ended up with more than one vendor ID, the same street address appears under each ID, so I don't think the name matching joined unrelated firms. Each firm's details come from its most recent Black American row.

**Decisions you may want to change:**
- **Expired certifications are included.** 328 firms are currently certified and 188 have expired. Each record keeps the firm's latest status, so you can filter to active firms only.
- **Three firms are kept despite a newer row with no race recorded.** C.C. Security Corp., Hope Plumbing LLC and KraneWorks Inc. Crane Service each have an older Black American row. I read "No minority race/ethnicity identified" as "not recorded," not as a contradiction.
- **One merge is uncertain.** "KINGDOM HOME CARE SOLUTIONS LLC" and "IMPACT CONSTRUCTION, LLC" share a vendor ID and an address, so they are one record under the newer name.

**Other problems in the file**, all listed in `NOTES.md`:
- County is "NA" on every row, and state is blank on 5,176 rows. Where state is blank and the zip starts with 06, I set it to CT.
- Zip codes are messy. Some contain "CT" or fragments of other fields, and 4-digit zips have lost their leading 0.
- 34 rows have start dates after the download date, some as late as 2028.
- Some industry codes are cut short (e.g. `2383`), and 31 of the returned firms have none at all.
- The file has no owner name, phone, email or website, so those fields are always blank.
